title: Treasury yields highlight barriers to tokenized money market fund adoption
description: A November 21 analysis compares stablecoin and Treasury yields, while separate November 17 reporting says recent stablecoin outflows have not flowed into tokenized funds.
why_it_matters: Tokenized Treasury and money market products could connect blockchain liquidity with conventional short-term interest income, but investor eligibility, minimum subscriptions and redemption schedules limit whether they can replace readily transferable stablecoins.
keyTakeaways: CCN reports that analyst Jamie Coutts observed an inverse historical relationship between stablecoin supply changes and Treasury bill yields, not proof of capital rotation.
CCN cites a November 12 DeFi yield comparison in which 48 of 98 large stablecoin pools exceeded the Treasury bill benchmark.
Bloomingbit reported on November 17 that Coutts viewed a recent $17 billion stablecoin contraction as capital leaving crypto, not moving into tokenized money market funds.
body:
Higher yields on short-dated US government debt are renewing questions about the opportunity cost of holding non-interest-bearing stablecoins. In a November 21 analysis, CCN reported analyst Jamie Coutts' estimate of a negative 0.62 correlation between changes in stablecoin supply and Treasury bill yields since 2022. That historical association does not establish that investors are switching directly into tokenized funds.

CCN also cited a DefiLlama study published November 12. The study examined 98 large stablecoin pools without token incentives, reporting a median base yield of 4.07%, compared with a 4.17% three-month Treasury bill benchmark measured earlier in November. Forty-eight pools exceeded that benchmark, although higher returns can carry additional credit, smart-contract and liquidity risks.

Separate November 17 reporting by Bloomingbit described Coutts' view that stablecoin supply had fallen by $17 billion since August, with funds leaving the crypto market rather than rotating into tokenized money market products. Tokenized funds can offer exposure to Treasury income, but subscription thresholds, investor restrictions and redemption windows can prevent them from serving as immediate substitutes for liquid payment tokens. The potential migration remains a hypothesis, not a documented inflow.

CCN reports that 48 of the examined stablecoin pools outperformed the three-month Treasury bill benchmark.

Bloomingbit reported Coutts' assessment that stablecoin outflows were leaving the crypto market rather than entering tokenized money market funds.
